facts.statement: Shakajlura is an extinct genus containing only one known species, which is recognized from a partial skull and fragmentary skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Shakajlura riojanensis, known from a partial skull and fragmentary skeleton.

facts.statement: Shakajlura riojanensis was described as a new genus and species by Ariel F. Cardillo and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Ariel F. Cardillo and colleagues described Shakajlura riojanensis as a new genus and species of paracrocodylomorph

facts.statement: Shakajlura lived during the Ladinian to Carnian ages of the Triassic period.
The time range for Shakajlura is estimated to be between 241.464 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Carnian (241.464 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Shakajlura fossils were found in the Tarjadia Assemblage Zone of the Chañares Formation in La Rioja Province, northwestern Argentina.
Shakajlura is considered probably an early-diverging member of the clade Paracrocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: Notes: Probably an early-diverging member of Paracrocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: While Shakajlura is recovered as an early-diverging paracrocodylomorph, researchers note that the possibility of it being an early-diverging member of Loricata cannot be discarded.
Shakajlura is considered a new component among the top predators of the Chañares Formation.

rejected.statement: Fossils of Shakajlura were discovered during fieldwork in the autumns of 2017 and 2018 at the Campo Cordoba Norte locality.
rejected.quote: The Shakajlura fossil material was discovered during fieldwork in the autumns of 2017 and 2018 in the Campo Cordoba Norte locality of the Chañares Formation
